statement: Call another Grasshopper definition as a function whose inputs and outputs are derived from its Get and Context components.
superiority: Typed function signatures with versioning and instant rename-safe refactoring.

acceptance.corpus: Definition with 3 inputs and 2 outputs called from a parent definition
acceptance.tolerance: Outputs equal direct run bit-for-bit on 100 random inputs

statement: Discover a function's inputs and outputs once, then solve repeatedly using an identifier instead of resending the definition.
superiority: Content-hash identified definitions and binary payloads for lower overhead.

acceptance.tolerance: Definition transferred once; per-call overhead <= 5 ms on loopback

statement: Configure each function input with prompt text, enablement, item/list/tree access and minimum/maximum value counts.

source.ref: Get component access (item, list, tree, min/max)

superiority: Validate input shape at the call site with clear errors.

acceptance.corpus: Calls with item, list and tree data and out-of-range counts
acceptance.tolerance: Valid shapes accepted; invalid rejected with message

statement: Pass whole data trees to a function and solve each branch in its own parallel process.

source.ref: Data tree input with per-branch parallel solving

superiority: Deterministic result ordering regardless of parallel completion order.

acceptance.tolerance: Output tree identical to serial run; >= 3x speedup on 8 cores

statement: Point a call to a local file, remote machine address or REST endpoint, and optionally expose the path as a canvas input.

source.ref: Function path (local file, URL, REST endpoint)

superiority: Path resolution with relative paths and missing-file diagnostics.

acceptance.corpus: Call resolved from file, URL and endpoint
acceptance.tolerance: All resolve to equal results; broken path gives named error

statement: Configure compute server URLs, an API key, concurrent request limit and child process count, and auto-start a local server.

source.ref: Server preferences (URL, API key, concurrency, child count)

superiority: Zero-configuration local solving with settings validated before first call.

acceptance.tolerance: First call succeeds without manual settings

statement: Cache previous results locally so repeated identical inputs return instantly.
superiority: Content-addressed cache with size limit and per-function invalidation.

acceptance.tolerance: Cache hit rate 98%; hit latency <= 1 ms

statement: Cache results on a remote Hops server so different users share previous solutions.
superiority: Shared cache keyed by definition hash and inputs with TTL.

acceptance.tolerance: Second client served from cache with >= 90% hits

statement: Keep the interface responsive during long remote solves and update the document when results arrive, with a cap on parallel requests.
superiority: Cancel in-flight solves when inputs change.

acceptance.tolerance: UI frame time <= 16 ms; stale results discarded

statement: Define function outputs with Context Bake and Print components whose input names become output names.
superiority: Typed outputs including geometry, text and tables.

acceptance.tolerance: Names and types match; values equal direct run

statement: Serve Python functions with scientific libraries to Grasshopper over HTTP, supporting parallel runs and breakpoint debugging.
superiority: Built-in Python functions with no separate server process.

acceptance.corpus: Numeric function using matrix solve called 1,000 times
acceptance.tolerance: Results within 1e-12 of reference; sub-10 ms per call

statement: Call geometry operations such as intersection, meshing, boolean and mass properties over a stateless REST API from other languages.
superiority: Same operations exposed through the Dino scripting API and REST with identical results.

acceptance.corpus: 100 boolean and mass-property calls through REST
acceptance.tolerance: Volume within 1e-9 relative of local call

statement: Extend the server by registering static plug-in methods as new endpoints with automatic data conversion.
superiority: Hot-reload of endpoint plug-ins without server restart.

acceptance.tolerance: Endpoints listed in the SDK page and return correct results

statement: Run a pool of worker processes, each solving one definition at a time, with queueing, idle shutdown and optional warm-up.

source.ref: Child process pool and idle management

superiority: Shared-memory workers with sub-second warm start.

acceptance.tolerance: No failures; cold start <= 2 s; queue wait reported

statement: Configure port, number of children, spawn-on-startup and idle time-out for a production server.

source.ref: Deployment settings (port, child count, idle span, spawn on startup)

superiority: Settings applied live with validation instead of server restart.

acceptance.corpus: Change of child count 4 to 8 under load

statement: Require a private key header on every request, serve over HTTPS and block access to internal network addresses.
superiority: Scoped, revocable keys with per-key rate limits.

acceptance.corpus: 1,000 requests, half with a wrong key
acceptance.tolerance: All unauthenticated refused with 401; none reach workers

statement: Expose endpoints for version, health check, active children and an SDK listing to verify a running server.
superiority: Prometheus-style metrics with queue depth and timings.

acceptance.tolerance: All return valid status within 100 ms

statement: Compress large responses and enforce configurable request size and timeout limits.
superiority: Streaming binary encoding for large meshes.

acceptance.tolerance: Compressed size <= 40% of raw; limits enforced with named error

statement: Run the server on Linux and cloud virtual machines with core-hour billing visibility.
superiority: Single container image with no per-core licence metering.
